theme: How many pursuers to catch one evader
title: Corner Patrol: Dismantling a Graph to Trap an Evader
mutation: composite: replace the decision goal (is the graph cop-win / what is its exact cop number) with an open-ended minimization goal (minimize total sum-of-squared guard-set size over a full elimination/dismantling certificate), and generalize the classical single-guard corner-domination rule to teams of guards of solver-chosen size, so the optimal team size at each vertex is itself part of the search space.
strategies: trivial: fixed deepest-first BFS elimination order, guard every vertex with ALL of its currently-live neighbors (always valid, no attempt to exploit redundancy)

greedy: same fixed order, but first try the classical single-guard corner test (is there one live neighbor whose closed neighborhood covers v's?); fall back to the full-neighbor guard whenever no single dominator exists

strong: same fixed order, but at each vertex run a greedy set-cover search over its live neighbors to find a small guard set exploiting neighbors that are already shadowed by other neighbors (the retract/corner-decomposition insight), never worse than the full-neighbor fallback and often far smaller on planted redundant-neighborhood gadgets
invalid: reports a guard set that leaves an escape route uncovered (deliberately infeasible)
